# Test if adding a sleep exposes the stampede issue
import subprocess
test_code = '''
import cachetools.func
from cachetools.func import lru_cache
import concurrent.futures
import time

call_count = [0]

@lru_cache(maxsize=10)
def compute(n):
    call_count[0] += 1
    time.sleep(0.1)  # Force concurrency
    return n * 5

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10) as executor:
    futures = [executor.submit(compute, 7) for _ in range(20)]
    results = [f.result() for f in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures)]

print(f"Results all equal: {all(r == 35 for r in results)}")
print(f"Call count: {call_count[0]}")
'''
result = subprocess.run(['python', '-c', test_code], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
